problem:
A body of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}$ meters.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=5$ seconds.
worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}+{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4t-{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4-(-{e}^{5-t}) \\  & =4+{e}^{5-t}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=5\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =4+{e}^{5-5} \\  & =4+1 \\  & =5\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =4\cdot (5) \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F|=|20|=20\,\text{N}.
$$
